title: 40 Minutes of Real English Listening Practice for B1-B2 | Improve Your English Just by Listening
article:
In this long, friendly conversation, Alice and David explain why listening is one of the best ways to learn English. They compare adult learners to babies. Babies listen for months before they say a single word, and our brains can also learn the patterns and rhythm of English just by hearing it again and again. The goal, they say, is to sound natural, not perfect. Even native speakers make mistakes, so learners should not be afraid of them.

The hosts then share three listening tips. First, listen actively: instead of reading subtitles in your own language, use English subtitles or none at all. Second, listen to things you enjoy, because when you are bored, your brain switches off. Third, listen every day, even for five minutes. Consistency matters more than quantity, just like watering a plant.

Next, they talk about daily life. Alice checks the news in the morning and then enjoys a slow coffee ritual, while David often skips breakfast. They describe their hobbies, from reading and cooking to thrillers that keep you on the edge of your seat, and they remember trips to Japan, Colombia and Peru, where people were warm and welcoming.

The middle of the video is full of useful language: casual phrases like "Hang on a second" and "I'm just going to...", polite work English such as "I wanted to follow up on our meeting" and "I look forward to hearing from you", words for feelings like grumpy and overwhelmed, and idioms such as "hit the nail on the head" and "bite off more than you can chew."

Finally, they discuss health and future goals. Eat everything in moderation, drink enough water, and set achievable goals. Above all, keep practising a little every day.
summary_zh: Alice 和 David 說明為什麼「聽」是學英文最有效的方法之一：像嬰兒一樣，先大量聽，大腦就會抓到英文的節奏與規律。
目標是說得自然，不是完美；連母語人士都會犯錯，不必害怕。
三個聽力技巧：主動聽（改用英文字幕或不開字幕）、聽自己喜歡的內容、每天聽，持續比份量重要。
影片中段教了大量實用說法：日常口語、職場 email 用語、描述情緒的字，以及常見慣用語。
最後談健康與目標：凡事適度、多喝水、設定做得到的目標，每天練一點英文。

vocab.quote: If you are bored, your brain switches off.
vocab.example: I always switch off when the meeting is too long.
Reading before bed is my evening ritual.

vocab.quote: Soup in winter is so comforting.
vocab.example: It's comforting to know that you're not alone.

vocab.word: on the edge of your seat
vocab.zh: 緊張刺激得坐不住；看得很入迷
vocab.quote: Yes, a thriller keeps you on the edge of your seat.
vocab.example: The last ten minutes of the game kept everyone on the edge of their seats.

vocab.quote: "Hang on a second. I didn't catch that."
vocab.example: Hang on a second, let me find my keys.

vocab.zh: 熱情好客的；讓人感到賓至如歸的
vocab.quote: The people were so warm, so friendly, very welcoming.
vocab.example: The hotel staff were very welcoming.

vocab.zh: 追蹤；後續跟進（之前談過的事）
vocab.quote: I wanted to follow up on our meeting last week.
vocab.example: I'm writing to follow up on my job application.

vocab.quote: Or, I look forward to hearing from you.
vocab.example: I'm looking forward to seeing you next week.
He's always grumpy before his first cup of coffee.

vocab.zh: 不知所措的；被壓得喘不過氣的
vocab.quote: Or I'm overwhelmed. There is too much, too many things.
vocab.example: I felt overwhelmed on my first day at the new job.

vocab.word: hit the nail on the head
vocab.zh: 一針見血；說得完全正確
vocab.quote: Oh, yes. You hit the nail on the head.
vocab.example: You hit the nail on the head: we need more time, not more money.

vocab.word: bite off more than you can chew
vocab.kk: [baɪt ɔf mor ðæn ju kæn tʃu]
vocab.zh: 承擔超過自己能力的事；貪多嚼不爛
vocab.quote: Bite off more than you can chew.
vocab.example: I bit off more than I could chew when I took three classes and a part-time job.
Coffee is fine if you drink it in moderation.
Set small, achievable goals for each week.

vocab.zh: 持續性；一貫性（規律地做）
vocab.example: Consistency is the key to learning a language.

shadowing.text: Yes, a thriller keeps you on the edge of your seat.
Yes, or if someone is talking too fast, "Hang on a second. I didn't catch that."
The stopping is worse than the mistake.
Yes, I wanted to follow up on our meeting last week.

mcq.q: I'm in a bad mood. Feeling negative or grumpy. 句中的 grumpy 最接近哪個意思？
mcq.explain: 影片 [26:01] 解釋 grumpy = a little bit angry, irritated, like you don't want to talk to anyone。不是「想睡」，雖然早上常常又累又 grumpy。

mcq.q: I have a hundred things to do and don't know where to start. I'm ______. 最適合填哪個字？
mcq.explain: overwhelmed = 事情太多、承受不了、不知所措（影片 [27:04]）。welcoming 形容人或地方熱情好客；achievable 形容目標做得到；comforting 是令人安慰的。

mcq.word: hit the nail on the head
mcq.q: 朋友說：「我覺得問題是我們練習不夠。」你回：You hit the nail on the head. 這是什麼意思？
mcq.explain: hit the nail on the head 原意是「釘子正好打在頭上」，比喻說話一針見血、完全說中。影片 [28:44]：you said exactly the right thing。

mcq.word: bite off more than you can chew
mcq.q: He agreed to work three jobs at the same time. He bit off more than he could chew. 意思是？
options: 他承擔了超過自己能力的事
mcq.explain: 字面是「咬下一口太大、嚼不動」，比喻接下超出能力範圍的工作或責任。影片 [29:30]：you take on more than you can handle。

mcq.q: The people were so warm, so friendly, very welcoming. 句中的 welcoming 指的是？
options: 熱情好客、讓人有回家的感覺
mcq.explain: 影片 [18:55]：welcoming = they make you feel at home. They are happy you are there. 形容人或地方讓你感覺受歡迎。

cloze.sentence: Yes, if you are bored, your brain switches ______.
cloze.explain: switch off = 注意力關機、不再專心。影片 [5:30]。

cloze.sentence: After checking the news, I make a nice slow cup of coffee. It's my coffee ______.
cloze.explain: ritual = something you do regularly in a special way。影片 [8:32]。

cloze.sentence: I wanted to ______ up on our meeting last week.
cloze.explain: follow up on sth = 針對之前談過的事情再確認、跟進，是常見的職場 email 用語。影片 [24:09]。

cloze.sentence: You can eat a cookie, just not 10 cookies. Everything in ______.
cloze.explain: everything in moderation = 凡事適度、不過量。影片 [31:46]。
Consistency = 規律地持續做；quantity = 份量多少。每天練一點，比一天練很久然後停一週更有效。影片 [34:11]。

translate.zh: 等一下，你講太快了，我沒聽清楚。
translate.reference: Hang on a second. You're talking too fast, and I didn't catch that.

translate.zh: 這週工作太多了，我覺得有點不知所措。
translate.reference: I have too much work this week, and I feel a little overwhelmed.

translate.zh: 我想跟進一下上週的會議，期待收到你的回覆。
translate.reference: I wanted to follow up on our meeting last week. I look forward to hearing from you.
